what: REDUCE_COL + BulkWaitBulkPop asserts the input CB capacity is a MULTIPLE of Ht*DEST_AUTO_LIMIT (chunk_size), not of the block shape passed. A chunk_rows x cols block with cols < DEST_AUTO_LIMIT (the design's cols_per_group <= DEST_AUTO_LIMIT clamp) trips the --dev assert / hangs. Neither the header doc for BulkWaitBulkPop nor op_design.md mention it; I had to switch to WaitUpfrontNoPop + caller pop.
suggest: Document in reduce_helpers_compute.hpp (ReduceInputPolicy::BulkWaitBulkPop) that REDUCE_COL bulk = Ht*min(Wt,DEST_AUTO_LIMIT)... and that the CB must be a multiple of Ht*DEST_AUTO_LIMIT, or relax the assert to Ht*current_chunk.

what: DestReuseBinary<..., DEST_TO_SRCA> folds the CB operand's dtype reconfig onto srcB, but binary_reuse_dest_init unpacks the CB through unpacker A for either reuse side; when the CB format differs from the previous srcA CB (Float32 b after bf16 x) is_unpacker_A_configured_correctly fires (dev hang) and production would unpack with the wrong format. The design explicitly prescribes DEST_TO_SRCA for the apply chain.
suggest: Reconfig srcA for both reuse sides in DestReuseBinaryImpl (or static_assert format equality), and note in chain.hpp that the CB operand always goes through unpacker A.

ref: op_design.md Dataflow Strategy (totals multicast: PRE_HANDSHAKE=false + gather-ready signal) vs mcast_pipe.inl ReceiverPipe ctor (data_ready_.set(INVALID))
what: With handshake=False the root's gather-ready send_signal can land before a slow core constructs its ReceiverPipe, whose ctor resets the flag to INVALID -> lost signal -> hang. The design's zero-fill-then-signal scheme is unsafe as written; the mcast_pipe docs do not warn that the ctor reset races an early sender.
suggest: mcast_pipe.hpp: document that without PRE_HANDSHAKE the sender must have a happens-before with every receiver's ctor. Design: zero only pad rows (disjoint from records) and have every rect core inc the gather semaphore after constructing its receiver — no signal needed.

ref: .claude/references/ttnn-python-utility-bindings.md (get_dram_alignment) / op_design.md gamma row read (two 16-lane chunks at +0 and +32 B)
what: No reference states the Blackhole NoC read rule that source and destination must share their residue modulo the 64 B DRAM alignment; the design's RM gamma read (stick offset 64T+32 -> L1 face1 +512) violates it and silently returns wrong data (PCC 0.5), caught only because the dev watcher aborted.
suggest: Add an alignment rule to memory-layouts / tensor_accessor references: on BH, noc_async_read(src,dst) needs src%64 == dst%64 (WH: 32); reading sub-tile chunks of an RM stick into tile faces needs an aligned read + local fix-up.

ref: op_design.md Circular Buffers cb_x_pass1/cb_x_pass2 (streaming: aliased) + Traffic ranking stall-shadow (reader prefetches pass-2 chunks)
what: In streaming_2d the design aliases cb_x_pass1/2 on one region AND asks the reader to prefetch pass-2 chunks during the combine; the pass-2 credit counter is empty so the reader's reserve succeeds and overwrites pass-1 chunks compute is still reducing. Needed a separate ring (x_depth*chunk extra bytes).
suggest: Ledger/design: alias only in resident_2d; streaming needs distinct regions or the reader must not start pass 2 before compute finishes pass 1.

ref: op_design.md Mechanism caps: DEST_AUTO_LIMIT = 8 with fp32_dest_acc_en
what: DEST_AUTO_LIMIT is 8 with fp32 only under dst_full_sync_en=True; the default ComputeConfigDescriptor (half sync) gives 4. The design's knob table never names dst_full_sync_en, so a literal reading of the default compute config silently halves every DEST-derived extent.
suggest: Design/precision-convention: state the (fp32_dest_acc_en, dst_full_sync_en) pair the DEST cap assumes and mirror dest_helpers.hpp's table on the host.

summary: Ragged 2-D split: host argmax Pr*Pc with per-core [i*Ht//Pr,(i+1)*Ht//Pr) extents as RT args; kernels keep nominal CB quanta (chunk / cols / cols*Kg) and narrow only the work: dense valid_rows x valid_cols x layout, reduce of(valid_rows,valid_cols), colsum pad slots zero-filled so the K=cols membership matmul stays exact, writer skips pad tiles. RM ragged col group: per-tile-row tilize<w> dispatch + pad push/pop on cb_x_rm.

Perf attribution via --profile + per-RISC/zone analysis (probes/per_risc_kernel_time.py, zone_times.py). (1) Ragged split with taller-Pr tie-break regressed 4096x320/4096x640 1.8x: per-core cost scales with Ct_core (pass-2 affine build ~2.5us per channel tile + membership generation ~22ns/lane on the reader RISC); verifier tie-break rationale was inverted. Wide tie-break (largest Pc) fixes TILE. (2) New kernels with the OLD 80-core split are already 21-48% faster on TILE: runtime loop bounds stopped GCC unrolling the per-T/per-chunk helper bodies over constexpr cols/chunk_rows (i-cache). Re-introducing compile-time shapes (integral_constant dual path) regressed again. (3) 80->110 cores: -3..-4% on DRAM-bound large shapes, +0.6..1.4us on small-per-core-work shapes (participant cost of gather/mcast). (4) MIN_TILES_PER_CORE 4/8 badly hurt tiny shapes (64x320: 8.3->18.9us at 2 cores): keep 1. (5) RM: reader per-stick bound; critical path = ceil(Ht/Pr); shrink Pr/Pc to the fewest cores with the same max extent -> RM back to baseline. (6) Floor +0.25us reader pass-1 / +0.2us compute: generic runtime-extent loops vs fully folded 1x1 block; compute ablations (FillScalar chain, streaming square, tilize dispatch) all flat.
